messages:
Maya: Ran a focused nsys capture on the FP8 fast path with INT8 fallback, seq_len=1024, KV cache enabled. Seeing repeated host->device dequant copies on cache hits that take ~25-30% of per-request time.
Liam: can you paste the nsys top kernel timeline? which kernels are hot?
Maya: nsys summary excerpt below:
``n
fp8_gemm_kernel           0.9 ms  |  180 calls | 162 ms total
int8_gemm_kernel          0.7 ms  |  240 calls | 168 ms total
dequant_kern_host_copy    0.6 ms  |  240 calls | 144 ms total
fp8_dequant_apply         1.1 ms  |  120 calls | 132 ms total
kv_cache_hit_handler      0.05ms  |  360 calls |  18 ms total (but triggers dequant)
```
Maya: NVTX annotations show pattern: KV cache hit -> memcpy H2D -> dequant kernel -> small transpose -> enqueue. That memcpy+dequant sequence frequently serializes the otherwise fast FP8 path.
Sophie: wait, on hits we still dequant every time? I thought we dequant once and keep on GPU. :thinking: 
Maya: we currently store KV compressed (quantized) to reduce memory footprint. Rehydrate does dequant on every access because downstream fused kernels expect fp16/fp32 activations. That was the initial design tradeoff.
Ash: explains the p95 spike after FP8 rollout. We compressed the cache but didn't implement GPU-resident dequant pipeline or fusion.
Liam: numbers: what's the p95 delta vs previous fp16 baseline?
Maya: baseline (fp16, cache stored fp16): p95 ~= 42 ms. FP8 + compressed cache w/ current dequant-on-hit: p95 ~= 68 ms. Roughly +60% at p95 for some request shapes.
Nico: throughput improvements when not hitting cache?
Maya: pure GEMM throughput for generation phase improved ~12% on long sequences, but app-level p95 regressed because of dequant serialization on hot KV access.
PerfBot: automated trace: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1769987654-1
Sophie: mitigation ideas brainstorm:
- keep a small GPU-resident dequanted copy for hottest KV entries (LRU) to avoid H2D per hit
- fuse dequant + transpose + reshape into a single kernel to cut launches and intermediate copies
- choose fp16 path for short sequences (seq < 128) to avoid dequant overhead entirely
Ash: I like fusion + small LRU. Fusion should let us dequant in-place and feed the next kernel without host roundtrips.
Liam: also measure memcpy vs dequant kernel cost separately; at small payloads memcpy might dominate.
Maya: measured numbers for a typical KV tuple (shape like [num_heads, head_dim]): memcpy ~= 0.18 ms, dequant kernel ~= 0.6 ms. So dequant is heavy, but memcpy is non-trivial.
Sophie: could we keep quantized KV on GPU pinned memory to avoid H2D entirely? Would still need dequant kernel but saves copy time.
Maya: yes pinned helps, but we still pay dequant kernel cost. Fusion would eliminate the extra enqueue/overhead and possibly reduce total dequant work by doing it lazily / in-stream.
Nico: any eval accuracy impact from FP8? we should gate rollout if quality drops too much.
Maya: eval on our 2K prompt suite: micro BLEU-like metric down ~0.7 points vs fp16; some tail prompts show ~0.4% higher hallucination rate. We've flagged model team.
Ash: sounds tunable. We could: keep fp16 for short or critical prompts, or auto-fallback based on observed score threshold.
Liam: action items?
Maya: I'll prototype a fused dequant+transpose kernel and run nsys before/after. Goal: cut dequant kernel + launch overhead by >=50%. I'll post timelines and flamegraphs in this thread.
Sophie: I'll add a routing tweak: when cache hit rate > 60% and p95 > 55ms, bias requests to fp16 path until mitigations land.
Ash: I'll implement a tiny GPU-side LRU for hot KV entries and run perf tests with hit mixes (0%, 30%, 60%, 90%).
PerfBot: scheduled perf runs: 1769991200 (fusion prototype), 1769994800 (LRU experiment).
Maya: will attach nsys outputs + quick flamegraphs here after runs. If fusion looks good we can behind-flag rollout.
Liam: great, this explains the regression. Keep notes concise in the PR so infra-oncall can correlate traces.
Maya: will do. PR checklist item: 'measure memcpy vs dequant, compare p95, verify eval drop < 1%'.
Sophie: :thumbsup:
Maya: closing loop for now 12 will update EOD with initial traces.
